rules.title: The project has a manifest
rules.description: PROJECT.md or artifacts/project-manifest.md records purpose, stack, commands, environments, integrations, architectural rules, artifact locations, and current state.
rules.rationale: It is the file a fresh engineer or agent reads first, and nothing else answers what this is and what state it is in.
rules.remediation: Where the project has no manifest, start one from templates/PROJECT.md. Where one is already present -- including one a bootstrap wrote -- complete it in place rather than copying over it, which would discard whatever has been filled in. Either way its content must come from what this project is; a manifest answering the template's own prompts is scaffolding rather than a record (Standard 44 R11). This run has not established which of the two holds.
rules.$assuranceNote: Existence is checked, and whether the file still reads as the template rather than as this project. Whether its current-state fields are CURRENT is not checked, and no automated check can establish that.

rules.title: Consequential decisions are recorded as ADRs
rules.description: An ADR directory exists — artifacts/adr/, docs/adr/ or doc/adr/ — and holds records for consequential choices, including deliberate deviations from these standards.
rules.rationale: A decision without its rejected alternatives is indistinguishable from an accident.
rules.remediation: Create artifacts/adr/, or keep the docs/adr/ convention if the project already follows it, and record the decisions already made.
rules.$assuranceNote: The evaluator sees whether the directory and records exist, not whether every consequential decision has one.

rules.title: Global mutable state is named, owned, and resettable
rules.description: No mutable state is reachable process-wide without a decision record naming what the state is, who owns it, and how it is reset. A named and documented configuration singleton or connection pool is global but not hidden.
rules.rationale: Hidden is the qualifier. State whose owner is nobody produces order-dependent failures that appear first under parallel tests and get fixed by adding a sleep.
rules.remediation: Record the state, its owner, and its reset path in a decision record, or pass it explicitly instead.
rules.$assuranceNote: A module-level mutable binding is trivial to find and says nothing about whether the state is hidden or owned.

rules.title: Established boundaries are not bypassed
rules.description: No layer or module boundary is circumvented because going around it is easier, and no circular dependency is introduced. A transitional bypass during a recorded migration expires at that migration's stated end.
rules.rationale: A circular dependency is usually what a bypassed boundary becomes. Leaving the boundary documented and believed while writing code around it means the diagram now describes a system that does not exist.
rules.remediation: Route through the boundary, or move the boundary through a decision record so the new one is what everyone works to.
rules.$assuranceNote: Requires knowing where this project's boundaries are, which is a project-specific fact no scan has.

rules.title: A capability is not implemented twice
rules.description: No critical domain rule is duplicated across layers and no second implementation of an existing capability is created without justification. A strangler migration is the exception and expires at cutover.
rules.rationale: Two copies of a domain rule are a future defect with a delivery date: the first bug fixed in one copy makes them disagree, and nothing records which is authoritative.
rules.remediation: Extract the rule to one owner and call it from both places, or record which implementation is authoritative now and when the other is deleted.
rules.$assuranceNote: Similar code is not duplicated logic, and duplicated logic is often not similar code.

rules.title: Dependencies are evaluated before they are added
rules.description: A new dependency carries a recorded evaluation of whether it is necessary, proportionate to its weight: a transitive utility needs none, a framework or anything reaching the trust boundary needs a decision record.
rules.rationale: Obligation-shaped rather than prohibition-shaped, because what the source forbids is adding a dependency without evaluating - so there is no prohibited artifact to search for. Warning rather than error because an unevaluated dependency is a process omission, not a defect in the running system.
rules.remediation: Record what the dependency provides, what was considered instead, and what its removal would cost.
rules.$assuranceNote: A manifest shows which dependencies exist, never which were evaluated.
